note: bounded implementation sequence for the next work series (one StructuralDelta per step, each closed, verified, integrated and re-observed before the next; every step names the blockers it addresses and the acceptance steps it enables).  The series does not begin until this structure is integrated and the structural check passes (D27).  D28: every step names the decisions it depends on (registers/decisions.json), the constraints it runs under (registers/constraints.json) and the assumption it runs under until the owner decides.

steps.goal: the immutable minimal seed (tests/closure/registers/seed.json) with its failure matrix: boot, promote on startup_ok, rollback on no startup_ok / crash / corrupt object / interrupted pointer transaction, restart during PENDING, confinement, recovery view, everything with the origin server stopped; the generated-app origin decision (D-2) probed
steps.exit_evidence: seed failure matrix all PASS on loopback; seed size and dependency census; P07 recorded again
steps.assumption: runs under D-1-a (loopback as the evidence origin), D-2-a (a second loopback port per generated app) and D-8-a (seed replacement only as a qualified origin event); durability and installation (K-02, K-03) are external rows the delta writes probes for

steps.goal: git-compatible objects, overlay workpieces, tree snapshot/diff, CAS refs and audit/retire as a browser library, compared with git on the repository's own tree
steps.exit_evidence: every tree id and diff equal to git on committed histories; two concurrent CAS integrations: one winner; retire never removes a referenced object
steps.assumption: runs under D-6-a (git SHA-1 identities, sha256 artifacts) and D-9-a (a recorded tree as the horizon; loose objects only)

steps.goal: the Factory law (model, paths, checks, the verify/integrate/reinspect state machine) as a no_std crate with a host membrane, compiled to wasm; verdict parity with the host judge on the f00-f28 scenarios; receipts name the verifier object id; a first generation manifest
steps.exit_evidence: the ported engine reproduces every witness verdict byte-for-byte; one delta routed inside a generation on loopback
steps.assumption: runs under D-7-a (literal path authority, decided): the ported engine reproduces paths.rs as a pure function

steps.goal: operation classes with Linux and browser adapters and receipt parity (schema 3: capability, adapter, adapter identity); the specimens, the corpus oracle, bundle verification and observe as capabilities the generation runs itself
steps.exit_evidence: the same fixture yields the same verdict and receipt fields on both adapters; the four specimens compiled, verified and observed inside a generation
steps.assumption: runs under D-4-a (the pinned toolchains named by the KERNEL_BUILD receipt); RUST_BUILD keeps a Linux adapter (K-11)

steps.goal: the first run of the language-evolution contract: proposed in LANGUAGE 1 - a version statement, a source-role statement (evidence never becomes source), QUERY_LANGUAGE_MANIFEST (ABI 2), an expected-forms diagnostic parameter, generator-based presentation equivalence, separate compilation by public contract - built as Compiler 2 on the host under S-RUST + S-LANGUAGE-LAW (version-change mode), qualified against the LANGUAGE 1 corpus with migration records, the derived unknown-keyword attack set, L38-L43
steps.exit_evidence: corpus-v1 reproduced or migrated row by row; corpus-v2 frozen; manifest-v2 derived; every new keyword refused by Compiler 1; LANGUAGE VERSION 2 declared only in the delta that activates Compiler 2
steps.assumption: runs under D-5-a (BUILD without a registry refuses) and I-39-a (a source-role statement); the C14 text (I-29) is the owner's and is not waited on

steps.goal: N qualifies a confined candidate N+1 inside the browser (Q1-Q7: manifest completeness, source provenance, compiled-object receipts, law self-tests, specimens re-verified by N's verifier and BundleVerifier, the re-qualification set from the graph, non-mutation); templates as recipe data so a host/JS change swaps a generation without a kernel rebuild
steps.exit_evidence: a synthetic bad candidate refused for each Q; a good candidate proposed as pending; the kernel identity unchanged across a template-only swap
steps.assumption: runs under D-5-a: the runner refuses a candidate whose BUILD carries no verified plan

steps.goal: decision D-3 by evidence: B3 implemented (RUST_BUILD receipts, identity == pin before import, two independent build epochs agreeing) and a measured feasibility probe of B1 / B4 / B5 with exit criteria (size, memory, time to compile the pinned workspace; identity or behavioural oracle); the boundary re-drawn from measurements
steps.exit_evidence: an imported kernel qualified by identity and execution inside a generation; a written measurement for each candidate or the reason it cannot be measured from this environment
steps.assumption: runs under D-3-a (B3 first) and D-4-a (the identity oracle); hosted-toolchain measurements that need network are external (K-05)

steps.goal: the foundation-closure experiment run physically: N -> N+1 with non-compiled objects changed, a deliberately bad N+2 rolled back, restart survival, evidence fed back into observed ASCII; the remote-sync boundary (L4) drawn: divergence detection, fast-forward push through the chosen transport, credentials outside generations
steps.exit_evidence: every acceptance step except 3-4 PASS with the host removed; steps 3-4 PASS or the RUST_BUILD boundary named with FC-7 measurements
steps.assumption: runs the closure experiment on loopback under D-1-a, D-2-a, D-8-a, D-9-a with SHA-1 objects (D-6-a) and steps 3-4 gated by D-3-a; the public origin (K-01), installation (K-03) and the browser update (K-08) are external rows recorded, never substituted
